workflows..github/workflows/ci.yml:
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main, dev]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main, dev]
  # version.yml pushes its deterministic child with GITHUB_TOKEN, so GitHub
  # intentionally suppresses push/pull_request recursion. It dispatches this
  # read-only gate against the child's immutable v<version> ref explicitly;
  # the resulting checks attach to the exact promotion commit.
  workflow_dispatch:

# Group the CI jobs under a single ref-scoped key so a new push cancels the
# full gate in one sweep rather than leaving a stale job running.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

# Least-privilege default (wish stable-release-security-gate, F18). CI only ever
# reads the repo — no job here writes contents, packages, or attestations. Any
# future job that needs more must opt in with its own job-level `permissions:`.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  secrets-scan:
    name: Secrets Scan (GitGuardian)
    runs-on: blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404
    timeout-minutes: 5
    if: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' || github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository }}

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@93cb6efe18208431cddfb8368fd83d5badbf9bfd # v5
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: ./.github/actions/ggshield
        if: ${{ env.GITGUARDIAN_API_KEY != '' }}
        env:
          GITHUB_PUSH_BEFORE_SHA: ${{ github.event.before }}
          GITHUB_PUSH_BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          GITHUB_DEFAULT_BRANCH: main
          GITGUARDIAN_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GITGUARDIAN_API_KEY }}

  # A 40-hex pin is not proof the SHA exists. actions/upload-artifact was pinned
  # to b7c4aadc..., which resolves to no commit anywhere; it passed every static
  # lint and failed only when the job first executed, taking down three
  # release-publish jobs mid-outage. This resolves every pin against the API so
  # that class fails here instead of in a release.
  action-pins:
    name: Action Pin Resolvability
    runs-on: blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@93cb6efe18208431cddfb8368fd83d5badbf9bfd # v5
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Resolve every pinned action SHA
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: bash scripts/check-action-pins.sh

  # The survivor gate — the same battery `bun run check` runs locally, plus a
  # build. v5 is a zero-daemon CLI over `.genie/genie.db`; there is no resident
  # database daemon, no TUI, and no generated tmux theme, so the whole suite
  # runs in one process with a plain `bun test` — no skip flag, no file
  # sharding, because the test harness no longer boots a database.
  unit:
    name: Unit (build + typecheck + lint + dead-code + test) — bun ${{ matrix.bun }}
    runs-on: blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404
    timeout-minutes: 10
    # Both supported Bun lines, every entry required: the Quality Gate below
    # needs this job, and a matrix job's result is `success` only when every
    # entry succeeded (fail-fast off, so one red line never hides the other).
    # The floor stays engines.bun >=1.3.10; 1.4.4 is the newest line (#3194).
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        bun: ["1.3.11", "1.4.4"]

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@93cb6efe18208431cddfb8368fd83d5badbf9bfd # v5
        with:
          submodules: recursive
          persist-credentials: false
          # FULL history, for the legacy-skills-catalog step below: that
          # generator walks the shipped refs (HEAD, tags, origin/main, origin/dev,
          # refs/archive/*) over every `skills/*/SKILL.md` blob
          # genie ever committed. On the default depth-1 checkout it would see
          # almost no history and regenerate an incomplete catalog — the exact
          # failure the script's header warns about and why it is not in
          # `bun run check` (#2942).
          fetch-depth: 0

      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@0c5077e51419868618aeaa5fe8019c62421857d6 # v2
        with:
          bun-version: ${{ matrix.bun }}

      # Pinned Node 22: parts of the suite spawn `node` (the design-review
      # evidence tool the fresh-install smoke runs, and the node-targeted
      # scripts under scripts/) and need a modern runtime — without this pin
      # the runner's driverless system node would silently skip them.
      - uses: actions/setup-node@a0853c24544627f65ddf259abe73b1d18a591444 # v5
        with:
          node-version: "22"

      - name: Install dependencies
        env:
          BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }}/bun-cache-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Build
        run: bun run build

      - name: Typecheck
        run: bun run typecheck

      # Rust (genie-v7-tasks): the workspace's rust-toolchain.toml pins 1.94.0;
      # this installs it with the two components the gate needs.
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@dc08e2af391d489dff6d14cf743e574f7d1229c5 # 1.94.0
        with:
          toolchain: 1.94.0
          components: rustfmt, clippy

      - name: Cargo fmt
        run: cargo fmt --check

      - name: Cargo clippy
        run: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings

      - name: Cargo test
        run: cargo test --workspace --locked

      - name: Lint
        run: bunx biome check .

      - name: Dead code check (knip)
        run: bunx knip

      - name: Skills lint
        run: bun run skills:lint

      - name: Wishes lint
        run: bun run wishes:lint

      # Gated here rather than in `bun run check` because it needs the FULL
      # history the checkout above fetches. The check is an additive union, so
      # it proves the committed catalog is a SUPERSET of what this clone's
      # history yields — it names what is missing and prints that limit on
      # every verdict.
      - name: Legacy skills catalog (full history)
        run: bun scripts/legacy-skills-catalog.ts --check

      - name: Complexity budget
        run: bun run lint:complexity-budget

      - name: Fresh-install smoke
        run: bun run scripts/fresh-install-smoke.ts

      - name: Test
        run: bun test

  # Stable is declared for Linux AND macOS, so darwin is a gate, not a courtesy.
  # Until this job existed the whole suite was proven on ubuntu only, and six
  # tests failed on every macOS host for a year without CI ever seeing them
  # (#2926): a hardcoded linux executable name, a host-shaped "foreign platform"
  # id, GNU-only `tar --transform` and `cp --no-preserve=mode`. The build +
  # typecheck + test triad is what is genuinely platform-dependent; lint, knip
  # and the inventory/complexity gates read the same bytes on either OS and stay
  # on the linux runner (which is also the only place `blacksmith` runners
  # exist). macOS runners are slower and un-cached, hence the wider timeout.
  unit-darwin:
    name: Unit (darwin — build + typecheck + test) — bun ${{ matrix.bun }}
    runs-on: macos-latest
    timeout-minutes: 25
    # Both supported Bun lines, every entry required: the Quality Gate below
    # needs this job, and a matrix job's result is `success` only when every
    # entry succeeded (fail-fast off, so one red line never hides the other).
    # The floor stays engines.bun >=1.3.10; 1.4.4 is the newest line (#3194).
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        bun: ["1.3.11", "1.4.4"]

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@93cb6efe18208431cddfb8368fd83d5badbf9bfd # v5
        with:
          submodules: recursive
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@0c5077e51419868618aeaa5fe8019c62421857d6 # v2
        with:
          bun-version: ${{ matrix.bun }}

      # Same pin as the linux leg: parts of the suite spawn `node`.
      - uses: actions/setup-node@a0853c24544627f65ddf259abe73b1d18a591444 # v5
        with:
          node-version: "22"

      - name: Install dependencies
        env:
          BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }}/bun-cache-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Build
        run: bun run build

      - name: Typecheck
        run: bun run typecheck

      # Rust (genie-v7-tasks): the workspace's rust-toolchain.toml pins 1.94.0;
      # this installs it with the two components the gate needs.
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@dc08e2af391d489dff6d14cf743e574f7d1229c5 # 1.94.0
        with:
          toolchain: 1.94.0
          components: rustfmt, clippy

      - name: Cargo fmt
        run: cargo fmt --check

      - name: Cargo clippy
        run: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings

      - name: Cargo test
        run: cargo test --workspace --locked

      - name: Test
        run: bun test

  # End-to-end proof of the v5 thesis: the full wish lifecycle runs on git
  # documents + `.genie/genie.db` alone, with no resident process and no
  # Postgres. V5_E2E_BUILD=1 forces a fresh bundle before the assertions run.
  e2e:
    name: E2E (v5 lifecycle)
    runs-on: blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404
    timeout-minutes: 10

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@93cb6efe18208431cddfb8368fd83d5badbf9bfd # v5
        with:
          submodules: recursive
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@0c5077e51419868618aeaa5fe8019c62421857d6 # v2
        with:
          bun-version: "1.4.4"

      - name: Install dependencies
        env:
          BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }}/bun-cache-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: v5 lifecycle e2e
        run: V5_E2E_BUILD=1 bash tests/e2e/v5-lifecycle.sh

  # The skills inventory contract (wish `skills-everywhere`, C6): what
  # `skills@<PINNED> add <local checkout> --list` publishes must be exactly
  # `ls skills/*/SKILL.md` in the checkout, with no nested SKILL.md and no skill
  # directory missing one. This is its OWN job because resolving the published
  # inventory needs a real npx, and the `unit` job above stays network-free by
  # design. The comparison logic itself is unit-tested offline in
  # scripts/skills-inventory-parity.test.ts.
  #
  # The source is the LOCAL checkout: skills@1.5.23 ignores an `@<ref>` suffix
  # and serves the repository default branch instead (verified 2026-08-31),
  # which made the ref-pinned form of this check vacuous on PRs. The job stays
  # scoped to same-repository events, like secrets-scan above.
  skills-inventory-parity:
    name: Skills Inventory Parity (skills.sh --list)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    if: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' || github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository }}

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@93cb6efe18208431cddfb8368fd83d5badbf9bfd # v5
        with:
          # Compare the SAME commit the CLI is asked to publish, not the
          # synthetic pull_request merge commit.
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@0c5077e51419868618aeaa5fe8019c62421857d6 # v2
        with:
          bun-version: "1.4.4"

      - uses: actions/setup-node@a0853c24544627f65ddf259abe73b1d18a591444 # v5
        with:
          node-version: "22"

      - name: Compare the published inventory against skills/
        env:
          SKILLS_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Only the ATTEMPT is retried, never the argv: the call clones over
          # the network from npm and GitHub, and a transport blip must not read
          # as an inventory mismatch. Listing the LOCAL checkout: a bare non-default-
          # branch SHA makes the skills CLI silently fall back to the default branch
          # tree (verified 2026-08-31), which made this check vacuous on PRs.
          attempt=1
          until npx -y skills@1.5.23 add "$PWD" --list \
            >"${RUNNER_TEMP}/skills-list.txt" 2>&1; do
            if (( attempt >= 3 )); then
              cat "${RUNNER_TEMP}/skills-list.txt"
              echo "::error::skills-inventory-parity: the pinned skills CLI could not list this commit in ${attempt} attempts"
              exit 1
            fi
            echo "::warning::skills.sh --list attempt ${attempt} failed; retrying"
            tail -n 20 "${RUNNER_TEMP}/skills-list.txt"
            sleep $(( attempt * 15 ))
            attempt=$(( attempt + 1 ))
          done
          bun scripts/skills-inventory-parity.ts --repo . --list-file "${RUNNER_TEMP}/skills-list.txt"

      # brand/, .claude/skills/automagik-brand/ and scripts/brand-sync.mjs are a
      # byte copy of Automagik's brand: --check exits 1 naming each file that
      # differs from the copy's record, is missing, or is not recorded. It then
      # looks at Automagik's dev over the network, which is why it runs in this
      # job and not in `unit`; that look only prints (a ::warning when dev holds
      # a newer brand) and never changes the exit code. `!cancelled()` so a red
      # inventory step above never hides this verdict.
      - name: Brand copy matches its record
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: node scripts/brand-sync.mjs --check

  # The DSH plugins build themselves on a git install with `node build.mjs`,
  # and both manifests claim `engines.node >=22.12.0` (#3275). This job runs
  # that real prepare under exactly Node 22.12.0. It is its OWN job because the
  # floor Node has to come from somewhere and the `unit` jobs stay network-free
  # by design: the test file is excluded from the default `bun test`
  # (bunfig.toml) and runs only through `test:node-floor`, here with the binary
  # setup-node installed, so the test itself downloads nothing. Linux only.
  # Deliberately not in the Quality Gate's `needs`: whether this becomes a
  # required check is the repository owner's decision.
  node-floor:
    name: DSH plugin prepare on Node 22.12.0
    runs-on: blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404
    timeout-minutes: 10

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@93cb6efe18208431cddfb8368fd83d5badbf9bfd # v5
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@0c5077e51419868618aeaa5fe8019c62421857d6 # v2
        with:
          bun-version: "1.4.4"

      # Exactly the floor, never a range: the test refuses any other version.
      - uses: actions/setup-node@a0853c24544627f65ddf259abe73b1d18a591444 # v5
        with:
          node-version: "22.12.0"

      - name: Install dependencies
        env:
          BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }}/bun-cache-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Run each plugin's prepare under Node 22.12.0
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          GENIE_NODE_FLOOR_BIN="$(command -v node)"
          export GENIE_NODE_FLOOR_BIN
          node --version
          bun run test:node-floor

  # Umbrella status check. Branch protection is configured to require
  # "Quality Gate (typecheck + lint + test)" as a required status, so the
  # job name MUST stay exactly that string. `if: always()` ensures this
  # job runs even when a sub-job fails/cancels, so the umbrella reports
  # a deterministic failure rather than a skipped status that some
  # branch-protection configs silently accept.
  quality-gate:
    name: Quality Gate (typecheck + lint + test)
    needs: [unit, unit-darwin, e2e]
    runs-on: blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404
    if: always()
    timeout-minutes: 2

    steps:
      - name: Verify sub-jobs
        run: |
          UNIT="${{ needs.unit.result }}"
          DARWIN="${{ needs['unit-darwin'].result }}"
          E2E="${{ needs.e2e.result }}"
          echo "unit:        $UNIT"
          echo "unit-darwin: $DARWIN"
          echo "e2e:         $E2E"
          if [ "$UNIT" = "success" ] && [ "$DARWIN" = "success" ] && [ "$E2E" = "success" ]; then
            echo "All sub-jobs passed"
            exit 0
          fi
          echo "One or more sub-jobs did not succeed" >&2
          exit 1
workflows..github/workflows/rolling-pr.yml:
name: Rolling PR Maintenance

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 * * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: rolling-pr
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write

jobs:
  maintain:
    runs-on: blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - name: Guard — RELEASE_PLEASE_TOKEN must be valid
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PLEASE_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set +x
          set -o pipefail
          if [ -z "$GH_TOKEN" ]; then
            echo "::error::RELEASE_PLEASE_TOKEN missing or invalid (HTTP 401) — mint a PAT with contents:read + pull-requests:write and add it to repo secrets"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Cheap read-only probe. Keep only status and quota headers; discard
          # the response body and gh diagnostics so neither can reach the log.
          probe_exit=0
          probe_headers=$(
            gh api --include user 2>/dev/null | awk '
              BEGIN { headers = 1; status = "unknown" }
              { sub(/\r$/, "") }
              /^$/ { headers = 0 }
              headers && /^HTTP\// && $2 ~ /^[0-9][0-9][0-9]$/ { status = $2 }
              headers {
                name = tolower($1)
                if (name == "x-ratelimit-remaining:") remaining = $2
                if (name == "x-ratelimit-reset:") reset = $2
                if (name == "retry-after:") retry_after = $2
              }
              END { printf "%s|%s|%s|%s\n", status, remaining, reset, retry_after }
            '
          ) || probe_exit=$?
          IFS='|' read -r status remaining reset retry_after <<< "$probe_headers"
          case "$status" in
            2??)
              if [ "$probe_exit" -eq 0 ]; then exit 0; fi
              ;;
            401)
              echo "::error::RELEASE_PLEASE_TOKEN missing or invalid (HTTP 401) — mint a PAT with contents:read + pull-requests:write and add it to repo secrets"
              exit 1
              ;;
            403|429)
              if [ "$remaining" = 0 ] || [ -n "$retry_after" ]; then
                reset_time=''
                if [[ "$reset" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
                  reset_time=$(date -u -d "@$reset" '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S UTC' 2>/dev/null || true)
                fi
                echo "::error::release-please-token.rate_limited the token is valid but its account's API quota is exhausted${reset_time:+; rerun after $reset_time}"
                exit 1
              fi
              ;;
          esac
          echo "::error::release-please-token.probe_failed HTTP $status"
          exit 1

      - name: Check for existing Rolling PR
        id: check
        env:
          # Read path is PAT-free: listing PRs needs only read access, which
          # github.token retains even under this repo's Actions policy
          # (workflow permissions read-only, "create and approve pull
          # requests" disabled).
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          # Check if open PR exists (dev -> main)
          PR=$(gh pr list --repo ${{ github.repository }} --base main --head dev --state open --json number --jq '.[0].number')
          echo "pr=$PR" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          if [ -n "$PR" ]; then
            echo "Rolling PR #$PR exists and is up to date"
          fi

      - name: Create Rolling PR
        if: steps.check.outputs.pr == ''
        env:
          # Creation is the ONLY step that needs the PAT: verified repo policy
          # is read-only workflow permissions with "create and approve pull
          # requests" disabled, so github.token cannot create PRs.
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PLEASE_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          # Create new rolling PR. dev == main (no commits to promote) is a
          # healthy state, not a failure — tolerate exactly that error.
          set +e
          OUT=$(gh pr create --repo ${{ github.repository }} \
            --base main --head dev \
            --title "chore: rolling promotion dev -> main" \
            --body "$(cat <<'BODY'
          ## Rolling Promotion PR

          Auto-maintained rolling promotion PR from `dev` to `main`.

          **Process:**
          - This PR is automatically created and kept open
          - Human reviews and merges when ready
          - Label `ready-to-merge` added when all checks pass

          > **IMPORTANT: Merge with "Create a merge commit" — NEVER squash.**
          > Squash merging breaks history sync between dev and main,
          > causing the next rolling PR to show all commits again.

          > Human approval required for merge to production.
          BODY
          )" 2>&1)
          RC=$?
          set -e
          if [ $RC -ne 0 ]; then
            if echo "$OUT" | grep -q "No commits between"; then
              echo "dev == main — nothing to promote; healthy no-op"
            else
              echo "$OUT" >&2
              exit $RC
            fi
          else
            echo "$OUT"
            echo "Created new rolling PR"
          fi
